directAnswer: To set up a virtual machine, choose a hypervisor, install it, and create a new VM instance with the desired specifications.
summary: This guide provides steps to set up a virtual machine across different platforms, including software installation and configuration.

sections.heading: Overview of Virtual Machines
sections.body: A virtual machine (VM) is a software emulation of a physical computer, allowing you to run multiple operating systems on a single physical machine.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The setup process can vary depending on the hypervisor you choose, such as VMware, VirtualBox, or Hyper-V.

sections.heading: Common Caveats
sections.body: Ensure your hardware supports virtualization and that you allocate sufficient resources to the VM to avoid performance issues.

steps.title: Choose a Hypervisor
steps.detail: Select a hypervisor like VMware Workstation, Oracle VirtualBox, or Microsoft Hyper-V based on your requirements.

steps.title: Install the Hypervisor
steps.detail: Download and install the hypervisor software from the official website, following the installation prompts.

steps.title: Create a New Virtual Machine
steps.detail: Open the hypervisor and use the 'New VM' wizard to specify the VM's name, operating system, and resource allocation.

steps.title: Install the Operating System
steps.detail: Attach the OS installation media (ISO file or physical disk) and start the VM to install the operating system.

faqs.question: What are the minimum system requirements for running a virtual machine?
faqs.answer: Minimum requirements include a processor that supports virtualization, at least 4GB of RAM, and sufficient disk space.

faqs.question: Can I run multiple virtual machines at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can run multiple VMs simultaneously, but ensure your host machine has enough resources to support them.

faqs.question: How do I access my virtual machine once it's set up?
faqs.answer: You can access the VM through the hypervisor interface or use remote desktop tools if configured.

caveats: Ensure your BIOS/UEFI settings have virtualization enabled.
Performance may degrade if the host machine is under-resourced.
